terms.definition: A mapping from a graph object, such as a node, edge, or entire graph, to a vector in a lower-dimensional space. The vector is designed to retain selected information from the graph, but it is not a lossless copy. Which characteristics survive depends on the method, training data, and objective.

A matrix whose rows and columns correspond to graph nodes, with each entry recording whether a node pair has an edge or, in a weighted graph, the edge weight. A graph with N nodes has an N by N adjacency matrix, so its feature layout changes when nodes are added.

A learning approach that operates on the supplied set of observations and does not inherently provide a learned rule for representing unseen observations. In the discussed comparison, Node2Vec is transductive, so incorporating new nodes requires recomputing the representation.

A learning approach that learns a procedure which can be applied to new observations, provided their inputs meet the model's requirements. GraphSAGE is presented as inductive because it can compute representations for unseen nodes from learned neighborhood aggregation and available node information.

A node representation that tends to encode where a node sits relative to other nodes in the graph. Nodes close in graph distance may be close in embedding space. This differs from emphasizing similar neighborhood patterns, and the tendency is not a guarantee for every algorithm.

A representation that emphasizes the pattern or composition of a node's neighborhood. Nodes in different parts of a graph can therefore have similar representations when their local structures are alike, even if they are not close in graph distance.

A sequence generated by moving from a starting node through graph edges according to specified transition probabilities. Walk-based embedding methods use collections of these sequences as contextual training material, so sampling choices influence the information available to learn.

A training objective that learns vectors by predicting context items associated with an input item. In graph applications such as Node2Vec, nodes encountered near one another in sampled walks can play the roles of input and context.

A transductive graph embedding approach that samples biased random walks and learns node vectors from walk contexts. Its return parameter p and in-out parameter q influence walk transitions, which changes sampled context and can affect what graph information the vectors capture.

An inductive graph representation approach that learns to construct node embeddings using information aggregated from neighborhoods. It can use node properties as well as graph structure, and can represent unseen nodes when the required inputs and neighborhood information are available.
